## Done

`app/ProductGallery.tsx:1` now imports `Image` from `next/image` and renders each product's image at 300×200:

```tsx
<Image
  src={product.imageUrl}
  alt={product.name}
  width={300}
  height={200}
/>
```

This follows the `next/image` pattern from `app/page.tsx`, with `alt` derived from the product name so each image has a meaningful label.

**One deliberate deviation from the existing pattern:** the hero image in `app/page.tsx:15` passes `priority`, but I did not copy that prop. Per `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/02-components/image.md:293`, **`priority` was deprecated in Next.js 16 in favor of `preload`** — the installed type definitions confirm it (`get-img-props.d.ts:25`), and this project is on `next@^16.3.1-canary.3`. I left it off entirely rather than swapping in `preload`, since gallery images sit below the fold and should keep the default `loading="lazy"` behavior; eagerly preloading three of them would compete with the hero image for bandwidth.

Worth flagging separately: `app/page.tsx:15` still uses the deprecated `priority` prop and will likely warn. The correct replacement there is `preload`, since the hero genuinely is above the fold. I left it alone as it's outside what you asked for — happy to change it if you want.
